correctness.rationale: For any two-date Brownian stopping rule the decision is an F_a-measurable event A of probability 1-q. Conditional future maximum gain is (S_h-D_a)_+ with independent half-normal S_h and half-normal D_a. Strict rearrangement uniquely selects lower/upper drawdown quantiles; direct differentiation gives H prime = f_a G_h and endpoints H(0)=C_a,H(infinity)=C_b. Uniform quantile sliding fills all intermediate expectations, and inverse-quantile calculus proves signed second derivatives and a symmetric strictly concave width with sole peak at q=1/2. Standalone mpmath code passed 291 independent high-precision identity checks and 42 positive inequalities; finite checks supplement analytic proof.

value.rationale: The naturally first nontrivial atomic law in a major distribution-constrained stopping problem admits a complete solvable two-sided benchmark not present as an evaluated result in inspected primary papers. Full exact attainable interval, constructive nonrandomized rules and a universal optimal weight for the maximal uncertainty range are mathematical information beyond the known implicit barrier principle. The theorem is not asserted to solve atomless or multitime problems.
